subject: DATA: anonymous sign-ins create real users/{uid} profiles - 96% of accounts are anonymous
description: Found 2026-09-08 on the operator's lead ('search for anonymous use'). MEASURED: 963 of 1000 sampled Firebase Auth accounts have NO provider and NO email, i.e. they are ANONYMOUS sessions. And FirebaseAuth.handleAuthStateChange calls FirestoreManager.initializeNewUser(user) with NO isAnonymous guard, so every anonymous sign-in creates a real users/{uid} profile document indistinguishable from a student's. signInAnonymously is called from at least five surfaces: dashboard.html:8359, join/index.html:568, lobby.html:1235, admin/dr-hex-button-demo.html, and kahoot-firebase.js. THIS EXPLAINS SEVERAL THINGS AT ONCE. (1) The operator's memory of 'users bypassing the sign in modes': anonymous auth IS the bypass - a visitor gets a real account without ever signing in. (2) The August/September signup spike (3033 + 748) that I read as bulk class enrollment: those are very likely anonymous sessions, not students. (3) The callsign 'completion collapse' I reported (Feb 93 percent -> Aug 0.2 percent) is almost certainly this, not a UX regression - anonymous sessions never see the modal and never set a callsign. I flagged that figure as confounded at the time; this is the confounder. (4) EVERY per-user measurement I took today - streak distribution, achievement holdings, callsign counts - used 4017 'users' as the denominator, and if ~96 percent are anonymous the real student population is a few hundred. The conclusions still hold directionally (0 accounts above the streak cap is 0 either way) but the RATIOS are wrong. DECISIONS NEEDED: should anonymous sessions get a users/{uid} doc at all? If they must, they need a marker field so every consumer, export, count and audit can exclude them. Also worth checking whether anonymous accounts can accumulate XP/progress, and whether they are ever cleaned up.
